messages:
sara: Heads-up — saw a big coldstart cost spike in eu-west yesterday when interactive notebook traffic hit the cluster. Thinking we should prototype a 'burst-buffer' nodepool: preemptible GPUs, very short warm pool (30–60s), and different scale-down jitter.

toni: Can you paste the timeline? how big was the spike? :thinking_face:

sara: Short timeline: at 11:12 a bunch of notebook kernels launched (approx 25 concurrent new GPU pods over ~45s). Cluster-autoscaler spun up regular nodepool nodes (3 x p8-preempt) but VM image + driver init added ~120s to readiness -> user latency + >2x token cost.

alex: ugh. so warm pool would give us pre-warmed VMs that already have drivers + containerd layers primed?

sara: Exactly. But we don't want a long-lived warm pool (costy). Idea: separate burst-buffer pool that keeps N warm preemptible nodes in a minimal state (no pods) and a custom startup script that only keeps drivers + docker layers loaded. If demand observed, we attach GPUs immediately. If preempted, pool replenishes quickly but limited to budget.

mariadevops: Love the idea. A couple of risks: (1) preemptible eviction patterns in eu-west are spiky -> we need jittered replenishment, (2) NVidia driver mismatch between image variants caused failures last month. We should pin driver and use a tiny healthcheck container that calls nvidia-smi at boot.

devx-tom: For detection heuristics, can we avoid pure pod-count triggers? Notebooks sometimes spawn helper pods. I propose: trigger prewarm when 95th percentile GPU-pod creation rate over 30s > 2 OR queue_depth_gpu_requests > 3 for 10s.

toni: Agreed on smarter heuristics. Also we should treat interactive (DevTools) differently from batch jobs. interactive gets priority into burst-buffer; batch goes through regular autoscaler.
messages_continued:
ops-bot: INCIDENT_SUMMARY: 2026-02-12 11:12 eu-west coldstart latency spike. Affected: notebooks; Cost delta: +58% token/GPU unit for 2m.

alex: Rough config sketch for cluster-autoscaler flags we tried in staging (feedback welcome):
```
--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m
--scale-down-unready-time=5m
--max-empty-bulk-delete=1
--expander=least-waste
--balance-similar-node-groups=true
```
This pool would run cluster-autoscaler with a separate node-group label (node.kubernetes.io/burst-buffer=true) and a custom webhook that prefers burst-buffer for pods with label workload=interactive-gpu.

sara: Also plan to add node taint: burst-buffer:NoSchedule and toleration only for interactive pods. That prevents accidental scheduling from batch jobs when pool is at capacity.

mariadevops: On scale-down policy: instead of static cooldown, we experimented with exponential backoff per-node: first scale-down attempt after 60s idle, then 2x, 4x. This reduced thrash during short spikes.

toni: Cost question — what's the math on keeping 2 warm preemptible p8s vs paying more token/unit during coldstart?

sara: Quick back-of-envelope: preemptible p8 ~ $0.50/hr (region dependent); keeping 2 = $24/day. Yesterday's coldstart extra cost was ~ $1.8k over burst window due to slowed throughput and duplicate retries. So even with preemptions the warm pool pays for itself on incident-like days.

alex: Nice. We also need to harden CNI init timing — some VMs were 'Ready' but Pod couldn't pull image because CNI plugin wasn't finished. Suggest liveness probe that checks both node readiness and network egress (curl to registry) before marking warm node as usable.

devx-tom: For safety, add a canary route: 10% of new notebook launches go to dedicated non-preemptible pool (slow path) to catch image/driver regression without impacting all users.

mariadevops: And add an automated rollback for warm pool startup script if NVML check fails 3x in a row. Rollback to previous image and alert #eng-ml.

toni: API changes? Do we need SDK flags so devs can label interactive sessions?

sara: Minimal change: notebook-service will set annotation `redwood.io/interactive-gpu=true`. Scheduler webhook will translate that to toleration + nodeSelector. Ops only needs to manage pool sizing + autoscaler.

alex: One more operational note: region constraints. eu-west has stricter quota on preemptible GPUs; fallback policy should route new requests to eu-central burst-buffer or spin classic dedicated nodes depending on latency SLO. We'll add policy: prefer same-region burst-buffer, else try fallback region (eu-central), else start dedicated non-preempt nodes.

ops-bot: ACTION: @toni create proposal doc with pool sizing + cost model; @mariadevops add NVML healthcheck script; @devx-tom implement scheduler webhook POC. Due: 3 business days.

sara: I'll run a 48h A/B in staging with 2-node burst-buffer vs baseline and report telemetry (queue depth, coldstart latency, cost).

toni: Perfect. If staging looks good we'll trial in canary eu-west next week. :rocket:
